blockNote: The dream scripts, the Master's Emblem F trigger and three screen effects of the dungeon scenes of the Mountain of Souls (file offsets 138516-138957 and 140042-140441, SNES $04:9D14-$9ECD and $04:A30A-$A498; the multi-area actors lie between the two ranges).
=== WHAT RUNS HERE ===
Meta types, all started by placement rows of the A0B scenes (area $0B = the dungeon, scene n = location $3D + n):

- $40 ms_npc_old_man_dream_021D14 and $41 ms_npc_old_man_dream_girl_021DF8: the old man's dream (A0BS03, location $40), rows $07 and $08 at tiles ($0B,$0E) and ($0C,$0E). The old man speaks and sends the hero back; $41 is a figure that only returns (RTL), probably the girl of the dream (OQ-I037-12).
- $42 ms_npc_mushroom_dream_021DF9: the sleeping mushroom of its dream (A0BS06, location $43), row $04 at tile ($20,$2E): a talk handler and a way out at tile ($1C,$31).
- $43 ms_obj_master_emblem_f_021E8F: the Master's Emblem F trigger in the underground lake (A0BS05, location $42), row $08 at ($01,$00): the hero standing at tile ($20,$2E) gets the item once.

- $10 ms_effect_hdma_bg2_shear_02230A (A0BS01), $11 ms_effect_hdma_bg2_wave_02237E (A0BS02, A0BS03, A0BS07) and $3C ms_effect_hdma_coldata_gradient_022457 (A0BS02, A0BS03): HDMA effects that rebuild their table every frame (COP 91, then PHX / PLX around the table code); see the part notes (OQ-I037-11: what each looks like on screen is not verified at runtime).
=== DREAM TEXTS ===

Old man: 'I will not leave you and go off to other places I promise. As proof of my promise, I buried my belongings in the Aurora Ridge. The Magic Armor, 50 GEMs, and one Medical Herb. I hope someone will find them.' Mushroom: 'This is my hometown. The mountain winds carried my spores and now we live there.' and at the exit 'Make sure you don t walk around in a dream or you will get lost.' Emblem F: '<name> found Master s Emblem F.'
=== EVENT FLAGS ===

$0707 the old man's dream was seen (set at the end of his speech, tested by ms_npc_grandpa_dream_rod_0218BF in the house); $1A05 the Master's Emblem F was found (set by the trigger, tested at its start). Item $2F = Master's Emblem F.
=== OPEN ===

The walkthrough (chapter 5): speak with the mushroom in the westernmost cell with the Dream Rod equipped, press the switch in the dream, walk left out of the dream, and stand on the northernmost point of the island for the Emblem; the trigger tile ($20,$2E) is the ROM's version of that point (not verified at runtime). OQ-I037-11, OQ-I037-12.

partNotes.ms_effect_hdma_bg2_shear_02230A:
HDMA effect of the north slope: the lines below a fixed top part are shifted by a ramp.

When: placement script (type $10, A0BS01); runs once per frame after COP 91.
Sees: setup writes the table at $7E:7800 once: an entry of $7F lines and one of $10 lines with value 0 (the top 143 lines are not shifted), then 80 entries of one line each, ended by a 0 byte. Every frame the loop queues the table (JSL QueueHdmaDirect, register $0F = BG2HOFS) and refills the 80 values with a ramp: the step is (scroll_bg1_x - $60) * 2, the value of each line is the running sum of that step, stored with its two bytes swapped (XBA).
Why: a perspective-like shear of the second layer that follows the scroll position.
In: X = D = slot; M = 16.
Out: RTL each frame (PLX / PHX keep X for COP 91).
Clobbers: A, Y, dp$00, dp$0C.
partNotes.ms_effect_hdma_bg2_wave_02237E:
HDMA effect: a vertical wave of the second layer.

When: placement script (type $11, A0BS02, A0BS03 and A0BS07); once per frame after COP 91.
Sees: setup builds seven entries at $7E:7800, each with count $A0 (repeat mode, 32 lines) and the data pointer $7900, plus a 0 end. Every frame it copies 32 words of the 64-word sine table ms_hdma_wave_offsets_0223D7 to $7E:7900, starting at word ((frame_counter >> 1) & $1F), and queues the table with JSL QueueHdmaIndirect, register $10 = BG2VOFS.
Why: 7 x 32 = 224 lines all repeat the same 32 offsets, so the whole screen ripples and the ripple moves one word every second frame.
In: X = D = slot; M = 16.
Out: RTL each frame.
Clobbers: A, X, Y.

blockNote: The fairy gems and the push zones of the icy areas (file offsets 138958-139089 and 139789-139912, SNES $04:9ECE-$9F51 and $04:A20D-$A288; the snow mountain actors lie between the two ranges).
=== WHAT RUNS HERE ===

- Fairy gems (types $3E and $3F): a COP 14 root that waits for a lair, sets up the gem sprite (shared_actor_helpers_bank3.code_01B161) and idles looking at the hero (shared_actor_helpers_bank4.code_022289). The talk handler gives EXP once and then offers to go back: $3E (switch $EC, A0CS01 tile ($14,$1D)) gives 300 EXP (flag $1E00), $3F (switch $D9, A0BS04 tile ($1A,$29)) 400 EXP (flag $1D05). Texts: 'I am watching the world. Here, take this. <name> received EXP!' and 'Would you like to return to the location of the Mountain of Souls?' with the choice Stay / Go back; Go back ends with 'Good luck then.' and COP 10 to area $0A scene $01 at pixel ($01D8,$0040); Stay says 'Return to me when you are ready.' (walkthrough: the fairy gems give 300 and 400 EXP; the text wording is OQ-I037-14).

- Push zones (type $39, placed once in A0BS01, A0BS02, A0CS02 and A0CS03): ms_obj_push_zone_setup_02220D stores the table of the current location in push_zone_list and push_zone_bank and kills itself; player_core.ScanPushZones reads the 8-byte records (x0, x1, y0, y1 tiles, then dx and dy words) every frame. All records here have dx = 0 and dy = +1 (a push south): the icy slopes that the Mushroom Shoes do not stop ('You will still slip on the slopes though.'). Tables: North slope $3E 3 zones, Aurora's Ridge $3F 2, the ice hill $46 3, Laynole $47 1.
=== EVENT FLAGS ===
$1E00 and $1D05: the gem has given its EXP (checked first, so that later visits go straight to the choice). EXP is queued with COP 38 as BCD ($0300, $0400).
=== OPEN ===
The tables carry no names in the ROM; the names come from the location ids the setup actor tests ($3E, $3F, $46, $47). The extents of the zones were read, not confirmed in the emulator (OQ-I037-11).

blockNote: The ice sliding of the top of Snow Mountain and the Ice field of Laynole (file offsets 139090-139788, SNES $04:9F52-$A20C): a marker scan that tells when the hero is on the ice, and the slide itself.
=== WHAT RUNS HERE ===
Two actors placed together in A0CS01 (top of Snow Mountain, location $45) and A0CS03 (Ice field of Laynole, location $47): meta type $3A ms_obj_ice_marker_scan_021F52 and $3B ms_obj_ice_slide_022007.

- The marker scan reads a list of (x, y, value) records for its location (ms_ice_markers_summit_021FA9 for $45, ms_ice_markers_laynole_021FED for $47; any other location: it kills itself). Every frame it compares the hero's exact pixel position with the markers; on a hit, value 1 sets scene flag $0000 (the hero is on the ice) and value 0 clears it.

- The slide waits for flag $0000 (COP 05). Without the Mushroom Shoes (item $22; COP 19 jumps unless they are equipped) and when the hero's animation is a walking one (table ms_ice_walk_anims_022032), it takes the direction of that animation from PlayerMoveDirByAnim (0 up, 1 down, 2 right, 3 left), blocks input and moves the hero 2 pixels per frame in that direction (COP 2F) until the flag clears or a wall stops him; then it releases input and waits again.

- A wall is checked at each tile boundary on the way: COP 21 / 22 / 23 / 24 when the hero is also aligned on the cross axis, otherwise two explicit checks of tile_type_map (a non-zero byte is solid) by ms_obj_ice_tile_blocked_0221FA.
=== EVENT FLAGS ===

Scene flag $0000: the hero stands on the ice (set by the entry markers, cleared by the exit markers). Item $22 = Mushroom Shoes (the walkthrough: the shoes stop the sliding on level ice; 'Once on the ice, you'll automatically go south').
=== OPEN ===

The marker positions were read from the data, not verified at runtime; which marker is an entry and which an exit in the game (OQ-I037-8). The hero's +$14 word that the slide clears is not named (OQ-I037-5).

partNotes.ms_obj_ice_marker_scan_021F52:
Sets and clears scene flag $0000 when the hero stands exactly on a marker.

When: meta type $3A, placed in A0CS01 and A0CS03; runs every frame (COP 91).
Sees: location $45 uses ms_ice_markers_summit_021FA9, $47 ms_ice_markers_laynole_021FED; any other location: COP 86. Each record is three words (x, y, value) at bank 4; the list ends with $FFFF. The hero's x (+0) and y (+2) must both equal the record. A match with value 0 clears the flag, any other value sets it (COP 09).
Why: the slide needs to know where the ice starts and ends; markers on the entry and exit tiles do that without a map layer.
In: X = D = slot.
Out: RTL each frame (PLX keeps X for COP 91).
Clobbers: A, Y.

partNotes.ms_obj_ice_slide_move_022072:
Stores the slide direction and keeps sliding every frame.

When: code_02201C found a walking pose.
Sees: the direction = PlayerMoveDirByAnim[hero animation id] goes to own $2C, the hero's +$14 word is cleared, input is blocked ($2F80 set), COP 91. From now on each frame: COP 07 with bit 15 clear jumps to code_0220B4 when flag $0000 is clear (the hero left the ice: the slide ends), COP 19 on item $22 jumps to the step when the shoes are not equipped, otherwise to code_0220B4 (restart).
Why: the direction is fixed at the start, so the hero slides until a wall or the end of the ice.
In: X = own slot, Y = player_actor.
Out: RTL (via the step) or the restart.
Clobbers: A, Y.
partNotes.ms_obj_ice_slide_step_02209B:
One frame of the slide: checks the wall and moves the hero 2 pixels.

When: every frame while the slide runs.
Sees: the direction in own $2C: 0 up (loc_0220B8), 1 down (loc_022106), 2 right (loc_0221A6), 3 left (loc_022152). Each branch tests for a wall only when the hero is on a 16-pixel boundary along the direction of travel: if he is also aligned on the cross axis, the tile ahead is tested with COP 21 / 22 / 23 / 24; otherwise the two tiles ahead are tested with ms_obj_ice_tile_blocked_0221FA. A wall jumps to code_0220B3 and ends the slide. If free (or between boundaries): COP 2F shifts the hero by (0,-2), (0,+2), (+2,0) or (-2,0).
Why: the slide stops at the first wall in the direction, never in the middle of a tile.
In: X = own slot (PHX / PLX around the step), DBR as set by the script.
Out: RTL; a wall ends in code_0220B4 (COP 27 back to ms_obj_ice_slide_022007).
Clobbers: A, X, dp$16, dp$18.
partNotes.ms_obj_ice_tile_blocked_0221FA:
Tests whether the pixel position at dp$16 / dp$18 lies on a solid tile.

When: JSR from ms_obj_ice_slide_step_02209B, one or two times per frame.
Sees: PixelToMapIndex of (dp$16, dp$18) indexes tile_type_map; a non-zero byte is solid.
Why: the slide cannot use the actor tile test when the hero is between two tiles.
In: dp$16 = x, dp$18 = y in pixels; X is saved (PHX / PLX).
Out: carry set = blocked, carry clear = free.
Clobbers: A.
